strength_convention: alpha = z * sigma_within, sigma_within = pooled within-group sd of the activation projected onto that layer's steering direction
why: The first pilot used a shared alpha on a unit-norm direction. Because residual norms grow with depth, the same alpha delivered 7.5x less relative dose at L26 than L4 and reached only ~0.05 sigma, below threshold. Calibrating on the within-group spread makes z mean the same dose everywhere.

H1_layer_dependence.test: Friedman across layers at matched z, paired by prompt (n=74)

detail.note: no difference at baseline, as required

H1_layer_dependence.reading: At matched dose the four layers behave differently, and the divergence grows with dose.

H2_signed_effects.detail: Within-layer Wilcoxon vs z=0 is significant at 7 of 8 strengths for every layer (e.g. L20 z=4 p=2.3e-05). But only the z>=0 arm was swept in the calibrated run; the negative arm from the first pilot showed no asymmetry at |alpha|<=2.
H2_signed_effects.caveat: A calibrated negative arm (z<0) has not been run, so the sign-symmetry claim is untested.

effect_sizes_at_max_z._note: mean paired change in logit margin vs z=0
effect_sizes_at_max_z.reading: L20 and L26 respond ~10x more than L4 and L12 at equal dose, so layer is a first-order determinant of steering leverage.

direction_quality.reading: the contrast is weakly separated early in the stack and strongly separated late. A single-direction-per-layer design inherits this; early-layer directions are noisy, which partly explains their small effect.

limitations: 74 calibration prompts; a 0.014 accuracy granularity is one prompt
4 layers only, all on the positive z arm
counterfactual-answer rate stays at or near 0 everywhere: steering moves the margin but does not flip the 2-way argmax even at z=12
no held-out evaluation, so no generalization claim
next_steps: sweep the calibrated negative arm (z<0) to test H2 properly
extend to more layers to check whether the L4/L12 vs L20/L26 split is smooth or abrupt
run the chosen configuration once on the evaluation split
